# PGmc disagreement map

GENERATED analytical view; source forms remain separately authoritative.
Reading coverage, analytical review and explanatory certainty are independent.

Core triage compares the recorded citation units and retains every core alternative.
Tags identify reviewed questions; undetermined cases are not settled historical disagreements.
Unknown attribution or date is a review outcome, not source endorsement or a PGmc default.

Citation-unit triage, feature alignment and explanations of divergence have separate accountability.
Position-support reasons do not certify an explanation of inter-author disagreement.

Core cases: 393; different_units: 17; insufficient_evidence: 198; substantive_difference: 2; undetermined: 176.
Core alignment: bounded_limit: 249; unreviewed: 144.
The catalogue below covers every case. Detailed explanations follow only where reasoning is recorded;
the linked source ledger retains the complete alternatives, arguments and verification limits.

Orel explicitly starts from a colour adjective; Kroonen reverses the usual direction because PIE u-stem colour adjectives were productive and proposes an ablauting animal-name paradigm. - divergence_explanation / morphological_argument (analyst_inference): Orel40-41's adjective-first statement and Kroonen56-57's explicitly reversed animal-first account differ in directional derivation. Kroonen invokes productive PIE u-stem colour adjectives and an ablauting animal-name paradigm; aligning his objection with Orel's position is our bounded inference. [Orel2003 pp.40-41; Kroonen2013 pp.56-57]
  Premises: Both passages concern the same beaver/colour connection; no direct rebuttal of Orel is claimed. Counterarguments/limits: Orel's independent reasons for choosing adjective-first direction and the complete comparative paradigm weighting remain unestablished.

  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- descriptive_bridge / chronology (source_explicit): RT180 displays optional z in the PGmc stem and no z in the explicitly PWGmc endpoint; the latter is locally masculine. This is a dated descriptive relation within one account. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.180; RingeTaylor2014 pp.180]
  Premises: The full native optional token is source-proved, not an OCR restoration. It does not identify the undated endpoints intended by Orel and Kroonen. Counterarguments/limits: Whole-cell equivalence, the mechanism of z loss and the dictionaries' loan/cognate explanations are not established by this display.

Written present-root e/i differs between endorsed dictionary citations; Kroonen's rejected i is not agreement and Orel's long-i antecedent is another formation. Ringe explicitly supports short-i through following-j raising. Fulk supplies a j-present argument, not an authored PGmc word; Ringe-Taylor distinguishes underlying/surface and later finite cells with native-text limits. These feature/unit/attribution distinctions are reviewed, but common-endpoint equivalence and the inter-author cause remain unestablished.

- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Ringe pp.151-152 supply short-e ask intermediates before short-i PGmc present forms, and p.273 explicitly attributes the raised present-root vowel to j. [Ringe2017 pp.151-152,273; Ringe2017 pp.128]
  Premises: The source's ask etymon and short-vowel present derivation are distinguished from offer and from long-ī wait. This records a position argument under Ringe's stated conditioner; it does not back-date the intermediates or manufacture a PGmc e-bearing infinitive. Counterarguments/limits: Kroonen's defended e-bearing stem and Orel's long-i antecedent require their own representational and derivational premises. This does not establish why the authors disagree or complete the conditioning census.

- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Ringe173-174,252 and Kroonenxix explicitly use bind for inherited e > i before a tautosyllabic/coda nasal, with their different stated relative-date premises. [Ringe2017 pp.173-174,252; Kroonen2013 pp.xix; Ringe2017 pp.174]
  Premises: Class membership comes from named examples and syllabification, not a string match. Counterarguments/limits: This supports realised i; it does not state Orel's particular reason for e.
- descriptive_bridge / notation_convention (analyst_inference): Orelxii permits etymology/ablaut-based e/i choice; Ringe252 conditionally recovers underlying e beside realised i. Those allow a premised bridge, not established identity of Orel's specific bind representation. [Orel2003 pp.xii; Ringe2017 pp.252; Orel2003 pp.41; Kroonen2013 pp.64]
  Premises: Require evidence that Orel's bind e has the appropriate underlying/derivational status; his phonemic-opposition stance remains a separate issue. Counterarguments/limits: The method alone does not explain this headword or date it; no global dictionary e/i normalization.

Kroonen278, Ringe310 and RT205,231 reconstruct a neuter s/z-stem singular kalbaz; Fulk176-178 and RT385-386 retain distinct genitive/plural calfur and unresolved histories. Orel209's m./n. citation is not class proof.

- position_support / pie_reconstruction (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: Old s-stem with explicitly different singular/plural vowels; rejects Greek womb comparison on initial labiovelar and root-vowel grounds. [Kroonen2013 pp.278]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / pie_reconstruction (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: OE cealf is explicitly cited. Despite the initial-consonant discrepancy, Orel relates the word to Sanskrit garbha 'womb' and associated Indo-European formations; the bibliography also records an older s-stem proposal. [Orel2003 pp.209]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Kroonen278, Ringe310-311 and RT205,231 explicitly allow neuter z-stem singular kalbaz alongside oblique/plural kalbiz forms; az alone does not identify masculine a-stem. [Kroonen2013 pp.278; Kroonen2013 pp.278; Ringe2017 pp.310; Ringe2017 pp.310; RingeTaylor2014 pp.205]
  Premises: Selected singular, oblique stem and plural are different units. Counterarguments/limits: The original Anglian paradigm is not thereby explained.
- position_support / analogy (source_explicit): Fulk176-178 calls the rhotacism/syncope/parasiting explanation likeliest but challenges it; RT385-386 doubts iz/uz and levelling scenarios and cannot specify a father-analogy mechanism. Identical calfur genitive and plural are not one cell. [Fulk2018 pp.176-178; Fulk2018 pp.177; Fulk2018 pp.178; RingeTaylor2014 pp.386; RingeTaylor2014 pp.385; RingeTaylor2014 pp.385]
  Premises: Actual cell receipts constrain hypotheses; reported analogy is not adopted CAPR grammar. Counterarguments/limits: Further original-paradigm evidence is missing.

  Premises: Neither i-formation nor eu neuter is silently normalized away or treated as an unrelated precious-beast homonym. Counterarguments/limits: The intra-author formation/trigger/iu-eu bridge remains unexplained; no complete equivalence claim.

- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: PGmc preserves r/n heteroclisy; West Germanic generalized r, while Gothic moved the word into neuter n-stems. [Kroonen2013 pp.151]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: Cites OE fȳr with Indo-European fire comparisons. ON masculine i-stem and *furaz are separately noted, and the entry directs the reader to *funōn. [Orel2003 pp.121]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: The fire cross-reference reconstructs the old oblique n-forms of an r/n-stem, reflected by Gothic fōn and genitive funins; derives WGmc spark *funkōn from it. [Orel2003 pp.119]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Kroonen151 describes neuter n-stem incorporation while Fulk180 calls Gothic fire the only neuter root-stem and attests three cases. Ringe309 offers post-PGmc dissimilation/remodeling only as possible. Classification and chronology are genuine analytical questions, not established whole-row causes. [Kroonen2013 pp.151; Kroonen2013 pp.151; Fulk2018 pp.15,180; Ringe2017 pp.56-57,147,162,221-222,309; Ringe2017 pp.309]
  Premises: Complete cited argument; cell, source qualifications, stage, confidence and verification remain independent. Focused prehistory/front-vowel explanations do not settle the whole row.
- position_support / lexical_identification (source_explicit): RT119's water,225/318's wizard and318's cow cells are comparanda, not fire ancestors. Doubtful fuiri and nominal ui development do not quote the selected PGmc fūri or OE dative fȳre. Separate owned/conditional/reported head origins, comparative verbs/suffixes, expected plurals and actual cells; selected head input unchanged.

- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Kroonen215 calls haub newer than hab but certainly PGmc because of Gothic; a possible original proterodynamic hafuþ/habweþaz paradigm and oblique metathesis can explain it. Such a possible IE paradigm motivates doubt about Beekes/Boutkan non-IE borrowing; Orel148 only reports Beekes, while165 calls diphthongal variants secondary (taboo?). [Kroonen2013 pp.215]
  Premises: Complete cited arguments; date, cell, attribution, verification and confidence remain independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary paradigm dates and Orel's taboo premise remain unidentified; RT's conditioned suffix hypothesis is tentative and cannot by itself explain all PGmc variants.
- descriptive_bridge / analogy (source_explicit): RT257's conditioned i-to-u hypothesis and plural-to-singular leveling remain tentative, with heal/cure, calf, bless, strength and forearm independently matched.270 separates PGmc genitive, undated u-suffix forms and OE output.378's expected subtractive plural is not an attestation; actual identical, syncopated and unsyncopated plurals compete. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.257-258,270,377-378]
  Premises: Complete cited arguments; date, cell, attribution, verification and confidence remain independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary paradigm dates and Orel's taboo premise remain unidentified; RT's conditioned suffix hypothesis is tentative and cannot by itself explain all PGmc variants.
- position_support / loan_hypothesis (source_explicit): Fulk9 reports Boutkan's unusual uð/ið head-suffix alternation as a substrate argument; that is Boutkan's proposed criterion, not Fulk's own categorical borrowing verdict or an independently consulted Boutkan publication. [Fulk2018 pp.9]
  Premises: Complete cited arguments; date, cell, attribution, verification and confidence remain independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary paradigm dates and Orel's taboo premise remain unidentified; RT's conditioned suffix hypothesis is tentative and cannot by itself explain all PGmc variants.
- position_support / method (source_explicit): Fulk8-10 retains the Italo-Germanic parallels, reports the substrate proposal and identifies circularity in treating words selected for lack of an IE etymology as proof of unusual substrate phonology. The methodological objection does not prove that every reported loan is inherited. [Fulk2018 pp.8-10]
  Premises: Complete cited arguments; date, cell, attribution, verification and confidence remain independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary paradigm dates and Orel's taboo premise remain unidentified; RT's conditioned suffix hypothesis is tentative and cannot by itself explain all PGmc variants.

No explicit diagnostic establishing secondary n is given. [Orel2003 pp.193]
  Premises: Complete printed-page arguments; attribution, cell, stage, support and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary suffixal n and comparative admission remain substantive but their complete divergent rationale is unestablished; masculine/neuter, other honey etymon and late suffix i do not collapse into selected huniġ ancestry.
- position_support / reflex_set (source_explicit): Suffixal n is original and dissimilated in many daughters, retained in ON/OHG/Dutch; safflower and honey seem derived from brownish-yellow/amber root or adjective. Tocharian bee, Prussian brown and Sanskrit gold are formally problematic; masculine citation and neuter OE remain distinct. [Kroonen2013 pp.255-256]
  Premises: Complete printed-page arguments; attribution, cell, stage, support and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary suffixal n and comparative admission remain substantive but their complete divergent rationale is unestablished; masculine/neuter, other honey etymon and late suffix i do not collapse into selected huniġ ancestry.
- descriptive_bridge / sound_law (source_explicit): Northern intervocalic nasal inhibits stressed-u lowering. PWGmc honag/hunag are alternatives, not two successive stages. Unstressed fronting, palatalization and late e to i are distinct; suffix i reached its final stage after mutation and did not trigger it. Holy is a parallel suffix example, not honey etymon. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.30-32,152-153,211-213,334-335]
  Premises: Complete printed-page arguments; attribution, cell, stage, support and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Original versus secondary suffixal n and comparative admission remain substantive but their complete divergent rationale is unestablished; masculine/neuter, other honey etymon and late suffix i do not collapse into selected huniġ ancestry.

Surface/underlying, causative/strong and finite/nonfinite cells do not establish a complete shared root history; no missing participle is invented. - position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Optional j may reflect old third-singular klok-éi-ti versus third-plural klok-i-énti. Bird-cackle semantics are possible; iterative hlak(k)ōn, laughter noun and weak causative are different formations. This is a possible i-present explanation, not a dated PGmc whole word. [Kroonen2013 pp.228-231]
  Premises: Complete page-cited arguments; report ownership, cell, date and confidence independent. Surface/underlying, causative/strong and finite/nonfinite cells do not establish a complete shared root history; no missing participle is invented.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Strong class VI j-present laugh is not a weak causative. The causative long vowel is explained by PIE oH versus H, while other causatives may copy strong preterites. Original light laugh versus heavy weak thūxijan explains the apparent strong/weak syncope contrast physically; the303 footnote qualifies simplified PGmc presentation of ij reduction. [Fulk2018 pp.265-266,294-295,301-303]
  Premises: Complete page-cited arguments; report ownership, cell, date and confidence independent. - position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Voiced PGmc hlōgijaną causative contrasts with base hlahjaną. The strong VI roster supplies past singular hlōh and plural hlōgun, but no PGmc laugh participle. Source phonetic inventory and morphological rule presentation are not CAPR law adoption. [Ringe2017 pp.244-246,275-277]
  Premises: Complete page-cited arguments; report ownership, cell, date and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Optional i-present, descriptive/cackle and laryngeal quantity accounts are independent. Surface/underlying, causative/strong and finite/nonfinite cells do not establish a complete shared root history; no missing participle is invented.
- descriptive_bridge / sound_law (source_explicit): Most consonants geminate before immediately following j in PWGmc; r/z are exempt and ij is not silently treated as Cj. Phonetic gemination and underlying hj are separate simultaneous representations; their order relative to r/z merger is not secured by bleeding alone. Breaking and mutation concern later chains; native corrupt letters/slashes remain. Anglian poetic hlehhan and alternative morphology histories are qualified; the343/348 principal-part rosters leave the participle empty. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.50-53,176-178,239-241,342-344,347-349]
  Premises: Complete page-cited arguments; report ownership, cell, date and confidence independent. Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date. Individually aligned research; no scientific adoption or established whole-row cause.

- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Milk is an archaic feminine root noun. Szemerényi's full/zero-grade contamination does not explain Schwebeablaut; Bammesberger's inserted schwa is not likely because alh- lacks it. A verbal origin of u is more likely but not established: contaminated melulk- or reduplicated mel-mulkan- could dissimilate. Gerundive, dairy and iterative derivatives are separate evidence, not extra milk citations. [Kroonen2013 pp.364-365,374]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Medial vowel origin is unclear and connection to the strong verb dubious. OHG milih has its own melikiz reconstruction; weak denominal and giving-milk adjectives are distinct. Bibliographical crossing proposals are reports, not endorsements. [Orel2003 pp.266-267]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date.
- position_support / pie_reconstruction (source_explicit): Medial laryngeal-to-u is tentative, and milk is not probative because there is no clear root-coda laryngeal evidence. Separately, PGmc consonant stems include full-grade meluk-. This does not establish noun u by the tentative rule. [Ringe2017 pp.98,222]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date.
- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Continental miluk/miluh raising before u and the Anglian dative milc through milyki from miluki are different claims. The latter retains an ending alternative or -i? and informs high-vowel loss; failures of continental raising without analogical restoration remain acknowledged. Neither claim establishes a universal PGmc u-raising rule. [Fulk2018 pp.68-69,79-81,388]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date.
- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Milk i-bearing reflexes may reflect raising in inflected eCuCi forms, with earlier melukez and later melukiz genitives. This is a conditional proposal, not an explicit date for the full genitive. Contrastive i/e before u independently argues against a pan-Germanic complementary distribution. [Cercignani1979 pp.75-76]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date.
- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Usual WS meolc derives from meoluc from meluk. Anglian milc plausibly generalizes genitive/dative forms, through double umlaut or early syncope then mutation. The Campbell proposal of PGmc raising through u is contradicted by Anglian ten/mountain; certainty for isolated milk is unattainable. WS e-back-umlaut requires following u with l/r/labial; Anglian milc removal from that domain is separate. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.253-254,324-325]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Exact milk noun-u origin, relation to verb and selected z-ending genealogy remain unestablished; conditional genitive/dative raising and continental u-raising do not establish a universal PGmc date.

Dental versus s-stem remodeling details are unrecoverable; moon is family, not month cell, and absent mutated dative does not quote the selected singular ending. Individually aligned research; no scientific adoption or established whole-row cause.

- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Month is uniquely Germanic t-stem corresponding to PIE s-stem; moon n-stem is secondary from nominative mēnō, which could continue s or t nominative. The t account is usually preferred because of month, but dental suffix is only Germanic. Late German dental is secondary, not ancestral selected-ending evidence. [Kroonen2013 pp.365]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Dental versus s-stem remodeling details are unrecoverable; moon is family, not month cell, and absent mutated dative does not quote the selected singular ending.
- position_support / analogy (source_explicit): PGmc moon n-stem and month dental stem arose from lexical split of an inherited s-stem. Similar nominatives make remodeling plausible, but the details are unrecoverable. Do not treat the dental origin as solved. [Ringe2017 pp.224]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Dental versus s-stem remodeling details are unrecoverable; moon is family, not month cell, and absent mutated dative does not quote the selected singular ending.
- position_support / chronology (source_explicit): Actual index month has final i and points to dative antecedent in5.2. Unlike Anglian milk dative, no mutated month dative exists; final-high-vowel loss and possible analogy therefore require their own qualifications. Certain WGmc plural cells alone preserve athematic category, not exact selected singular ending. [Fulk2018 pp.79-81,179-180,388]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Dental versus s-stem remodeling details are unrecoverable; moon is family, not month cell, and absent mutated dative does not quote the selected singular ending.

- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Suffix-accent PIE mother yields māþēr then PGmc mōdēr by regular Verner development. Mother is among five inherited r-stems; direct forms were hysterokinetic but generalized weak suffix makes genitive/plural reconstruction uncertain. Do not replace the quoted accent with Kroonen's root-accent premise. [Ringe2017 pp.122-123,307-308]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Suffix-accent versus root-accent/father-analogy accounts need independent accent and r-stem premises; selected long ē, suffix vowel leveling and plural history remain distinct.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Prokosch's all-paradigm root accent is reported, with apparent Verner consonant explained by father analogy. Fulk discusses multiple r-stem interpretations and prefers Stiles's general account; mother plural mōdru/mōdra may reflect collective neuter origin, not selected singular. Gothic mōdar is reconstructible but entirely unattested. [Fulk2018 pp.173-176]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: Suffix-accent versus root-accent/father-analogy accounts need independent accent and r-stem premises; selected long ē, suffix vowel leveling and plural history remain distinct.
- position_support / analogy (source_explicit): PWGmc nom er and acc ar should yield er. Stepmother supplies actual compound evidence; root-back-vowel nouns replace suffix vowel by u or later reflex. Genitive ur persists, dative mother reflects zero-suffix-vowel ri. Leveling seems plausible but cannot be proved; OE plural without i cannot directly reflect regular inherited i-ending, and alternative remodeling remains possible. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.381-383]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. L-derivative and a-stem versus secondary Nordic root inflection do not independently prove full source-convention equality of accented selected word or all deeper labialization premises. Individually aligned research; no scientific adoption or established whole-row cause.

- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): L-derivative of ablauting nail/claw root. Nordic root-noun inflection may be secondary because all other Germanic reflexes suggest an a-stem. Weak nail verb is separate, not selected noun ending. [Kroonen2013 pp.381]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: L-derivative and a-stem versus secondary Nordic root inflection do not independently prove full source-convention equality of accented selected word or all deeper labialization premises.
- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): PGmc naglaz, PWGmc nagl and OE fronted/palatalized nail are distinct endpoints. The unlabelled fronted intermediate is not automatically PWGmc. Epenthesis is normally absent after palatal consonant in final Cl, with nail among examples; native negl not silently converted into dotted ġ. [RingeTaylor2014 pp.147-149,212-213,329]
  Premises: Complete printed-page source arguments; source attribution, cell, stage and confidence independent. Counterarguments/limits: L-derivative and a-stem versus secondary Nordic root inflection do not independently prove full source-convention equality of accented selected word or all deeper labialization premises.
